subject: Computer Networking
title: AI-Driven Traffic Engineering
description: A short lesson to help you apply AI-Driven Traffic Engineering.

hook.text: Traditional routing picks the shortest path. AI considers congestion, latency, jitter, and demand.

buildup.text: AI models analyze traffic across the network in real time. They predict congestion before it hits.

discovery.text: Instead of reacting to a full link, AI reroutes preemptively. Users never feel the avoided jam.

twist.text: Google uses ML to optimize global backbone traffic. Millions saved by maximizing link utilization.

climax.text: Reinforcement learning experiments: try a route, measure results, improve. The network learns.

punchline.text: AI routes traffic before problems appear. Proactive, not reactive.

quiz.question: How does AI-driven traffic engineering differ from traditional routing?
options: It predicts and prevents congestion before it happens
It always chooses the shortest physical path
It routes all traffic through a single central server

details.summary: AI-driven traffic engineering uses machine learning to predict traffic patterns and optimize routing decisions across networks in real time. Instead of static routing policies, AI models analyze historical and current traffic to choose paths that minimize congestion, latency, and cost dynamically.
details.whyItMatters: Network traffic is unpredictable and bursty. AI-driven traffic engineering adapts routing in real time, achieving utilization and performance levels that static configurations cannot match.
takeaways: ML models predict traffic patterns and optimize routing dynamically
Real-time adaptation avoids congestion before it causes problems
Google pioneered AI traffic engineering on its global WAN

faq.question: How does AI improve traffic engineering?
faq.answer: AI models learn traffic patterns from historical data and predict near-future demand. They pre-position traffic across paths to prevent congestion rather than reacting after it occurs. Google reports achieving near-optimal link utilization with AI-driven traffic engineering on its backbone network.

faq.question: What is the difference from traditional traffic engineering?
faq.answer: Traditional traffic engineering uses static MPLS tunnels and manually configured weights. Changes require human intervention. AI-driven approaches continuously analyze real-time telemetry and adjust routing automatically, adapting to traffic shifts, failures, and demand changes within seconds.
